transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... for a long time now, I've just had this heavy, low feeling sitting on me most days. I mean, I still get through my driving routes for work, and my volunteer shifts, but it's like I'm just going through the motions instead of really being in my own life.
How long have you been feeling this way most days?
I'd say it's been about three years now. It started right around the time my dad passed away, and... well, it just hasn't really lifted since then.
Have you ever experienced any periods where your mood was unusually high, you felt extremely energetic, or you didn’t need much sleep, even for a few days or more?

No, I can't say I have. Honestly, I've never really been the type to bounce off the walls or anything. It's pretty much just been the opposite... just feeling drained most of the time. So, no, no unusual highs or going without sleep like that.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with others?

No, not really. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. I still like watching the game on the weekends, and I still don't mind my volunteer shifts or anything. It's not that I don't enjoy things anymore... it's just that heavy feeling I mentioned. But the stuff I like is still the stuff I like.
Have you experienced any other symptoms along with this heavy feeling, like fatigue, trouble concentrating, or feelings of worthlessness or guilt?

Well, I don't really have those feelings of being worthless or guilty, nothing like that. But the concentrating part... yeah, I've noticed a bit of an issue there. I mean, I can still do my job, but lately I catch myself rereading delivery times, or just staring at the schedule board at work a lot longer than I should. It's just... my mind doesn't really lock onto things the way it used to.
Have you noticed any days when your movements or speech slowed down, or when you felt physically restless or agitated for no clear reason?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't feel like I'm moving or talking any slower than usual. And I'm not restless or fidgety either. Physically, I feel pretty normal in that way, just... tired, I guess. But no, nothing like slowing down or being agitated.
Is your low mood something that you feel most of the day, nearly every day, even if it doesn't get in the way of what you're doing?

Yeah, that's exactly it. I mean, that's why I came in, really. For a long time now, I've been getting through my driving routes and my volunteer shifts without any real problems, but... there's just this heavy, low feeling sitting on me most days. It's there almost all the time. It just feels like I'm going through the motions instead of really being in my own life.
Can you tell me a bit more about when the heavy, low feeling shows up? Does it tend to happen after certain things, like stress or loss, or does it just seem to be there without a clear reason?

Well, it's pretty much just there all the time now. It doesn't really come and go with stress or anything like that. But as far as how it started... it's been going on for about three years. That's when my father died. Since then, it's just been this constant, low feeling that hasn't really lifted.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like watching games or volunteering, don't bring you the same satisfaction or pleasure they used to?

No, not really. I mean, I still like watching the games, and I still go to my volunteer shifts. I guess I still get something out of them. It's not that I've stopped enjoying things or lost interest. It's just that heavy feeling is always there in the background, even when I'm doing stuff I like.
Have you had days where your mood was so low that it felt like you couldn't function, or have you mostly been able to carry on with your daily life, even with that heavy feeling?

I haven't had days where I just can't function at all. I mean, I'm still showing up for my driving routes, and I'm still making it to the food pantry for my volunteer shifts. I can carry on, but... it's just that everything takes a lot more pushing than it used to. It's harder to get going. Like, there's this logistics supervisor job that opened up, and I started the application, but I just left it sitting there unfinished. I just don't trust myself to keep up with the extra responsibility right now with how heavy everything feels.
Even though you still do things like watch games and volunteer, do you feel like you're not getting the same sense of enjoyment or pleasure from them as you used to?

I think you might have asked me that already... but no, like I said, I still enjoy them. Watching the games, going to the food pantry—I still get satisfaction out of doing those things. The enjoyment is still there. It's just that the low feeling is there at the same time, if that makes sense.

Even if you still enjoy watching games or volunteering, have you noticed that those activities don’t feel as rewarding or pleasurable as they used to — like they used to light you up inside, but now they just feel more routine or flat?

Doc, I feel like we're beating a dead horse here. Like I just said, no, they don't feel flat. When I'm watching a good game, I still get the exact same kick out of it. When I finish up at the pantry, I still feel good about what I did. 

They haven't lost their spark at all. It's really just... that heavy mood is just riding along with me the rest of the time. But the things I like are still exactly the same.
